subject: Mutual action commitments: sprint playbook, owners & risk register
messages:
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@quarryhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Ruiz <evan.ruiz@quarryhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan and kickoff alignment

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — QuarryHealth is excited about Redwood's latency/cost profile for our triage assistant. Evan and I pulled together the high-level requirements from our side and would like to lock down a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and go-live window so procurement can sequence SOW and PO approvals.

High level asks from QuarryHealth:
- P0: Production inference for triage assistant (up to 4M tokens / month) with 99th pct latency < 300ms for short queries.
- P1: Prefix caching + warmup for predictable spikes during AM/PM shifts.
- Security: SOC2 evidence and KMS integration notes (procurement will need these attached to the SOW).

Can Redwood propose a MAP that includes concrete milestones, owners, acceptance criteria and cutover windows? Attached is our kickoff notes and a simple timeline we started.

Attachments: kickoff-notes.pdf, QH-requirements.csv

Proposed initial timeline from QuarryHealth: pilot in 6 weeks, production in 12 weeks. Open to adjustments based on your capacity/cutover risks.

Looking forward — please assign owners so we can surface to our engineering and procurement teams.

Thanks,
Alicia
Head of Product Operations
QuarryHealth
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@quarryhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan and kickoff alignment

Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and the timeline. I drafted a MAP and a first-pass sprint playbook that maps your requirements to milestones, owners, dates and acceptance criteria (see attached QH-MAP-draft.xlsx). Key callouts up front: 

- Milestone cadence: 2-week sprints with 3 implementation milestones (pilot, extended pilot, production cutover).
- Owners: Redwood will own model onboarding & serving runtime (Ben lead); QuarryHealth will own integration, traffic shaping, and end-to-end acceptance (Evan lead). Monica from CS will run runbooks and adoption checkpoints.
- Acceptance criteria: pilot requires 72-hour stability at 80% of expected load, latency SLOs within a 10% variance, and a smoke test checklist (see MAP tab).
- Risk register: I added three initial risks (quantization quality vs latency, warmup cold starts, procurement dependency). Each risk has a proposed mitigation and RACI owner.

Proposed dates (pending your confirmation):
- Sprint 0 / provisioning: Nov 8–Nov 19 (env + initial model sync)
- Pilot window: Nov 22–Dec 10 (3-week pilot, stability & metrics collection)
- Extended pilot / tuning: Dec 13–Jan 7 (model tuning, autoscale config)
- Production cutover target: Jan 18 (12-week horizon from today)

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm owners and any blackouts for the proposed windows.
2) Ben and I will circulate the SOW-v0.3 for procurement with an appendix linking SOC2 artifacts.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical handoff next Wednesday (Nov 2) — agenda: infra needs, traffic patterns, canary plan.

I attached QH-MAP-draft.xlsx and a short cutover-windows.csv with proposed blackout/maintenance slots. If that works for you, I'll push a HubSpot update to lock owners and milestones.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@quarryhealth.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-26T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan and kickoff alignment

Tessa — captured and added a few implementation-level details to the MAP before we send it to procurement. Attached: QH-SOW-v0.3.pdf and an exported cutover-windows.csv with explicit UTC times. Highlights: 

- Serving config: recommend starting with a 2-replica dedicated pool (g4dn-similar) with auto-burst to 4 for daytime windows. This keeps latency stable and limits cost during off-peak.
- Batching/warmup: we'll enable prefix caching and a 30-minute scheduled warmup to seed the KV cache before the AM spike. We flagged the quantization profile as optional in SOW (opt-in after pilot).
- Canary plan: 5% traffic for 48 hours then 25% for 72 hours before full cutover. Rollback thresholds defined in the MAP.

Procurement note: SOC2 artifacts are packaged in the SOW appendix; Monica, can you add a short paragraph describing audit log retention and our KMS partners?

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--- On 2026-10-25, Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and the timeline. I drafted a MAP...
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@quarryhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Ruiz <evan.ruiz@quarryhealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, procurement@quarryhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-27T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan and kickoff alignment

Tessa / Ben / Monica — this looks good and close to what we need. A few quick confirmations:

- Dates: Nov 8 provisioning and Jan 18 production cutover look fine for us, but procurement needs the SOW final by Nov 5 to start PO routing. Can you accelerate the SOW signature timeline?
- Owners: Confirm Evan as QuarryHealth lead for integration and myself as executive sponsor.
- Canary: the 5% then 25% ramp is fine — we only ask that the first canary be scheduled outside our nightly ETL between 02:00–04:00 UTC.

Action items for Redwood: please share the final SOW (v0.4) with procurement by EOD Nov 3 and add the SOC2 appendix link. Also, please send an invite for the technical handoff on Nov 2 at 10:00 PT.

We'll review the MAP internally tonight and will send any minor date conflicts by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — excited to move forward.

Alicia Moreno
Head of Product Operations
QuarryHealth
